text: Bravo, Bay Velichkov! Look, I like you this way. Why should we deceive the younger generation? Let’s show our cards. Ideals! Hogwash! Our personal earthly contentment—that is the ideal we must pursue. I am glad you have finally reached this truth. And does this vile people deserve for us to break our backs for them! While we were younger, it was one thing; but now—we’ve become men of forty years, we must think of ourselves. Enough of this meager living! Especially you, poor soul, you were completely exhausted in those Istanbul alleys, those Italian ones... wasn't that a whole feat? When you saw Stambolov go mad, you just packed your bags and left Bulgaria, abandoned those slaves—let them wallow in their slavery. They are used to it. You aren’t used to suffering, and like any gentleman, you made sure to bolt. What didn't you suffer in that godforsaken Halki—sometimes you didn't even have enough money for medicine. Bobchev and Madzharov kept quiet. Enough with the heroics. And you know what—go ahead and give up your godforsaken poetry too. It’s all well and good, but when the wind blows through your purse... but now, thank God, we’ve settled ourselves somewhat. They’ll start now, all sorts of kids, little socialists, little idealists, yapping at you, but don’t you even blink an eye! Turn a deaf ear, just look after your own pleasure, and while you're enjoying yourself, laugh at their wits. It’s well known. Why will they yap at you? Is it for some betrayal of yours, for deception, out of disappointment? No! Out of envy? Of course! Without a doubt! Without a doubt, out of envy! And why? Simply because their bones were crushed, their throats were torn, while you (you're a clever devil, damn you!) just dropped right into the warmest spot, all ready for you. Well, do you see now? Are you convinced? Didn't I tell you that in this world the best thing is to be nice and warm? This social struggle, ideals, and I don't know what other nonsense—it's all hogwash! Now, when you hold out your little bag at the end of the month and they shovel fifteen hundred levs into it... A fine thing, damn it! Hold on now! Once you've grabbed the bone—hold on! Don't you think for a moment whose skin those levs are being flayed from... Beat the flour sack, damn it all! Beat it! It keeps giving...

But you might wonder why I am writing you this letter. I am writing it to praise you for your speech the other day in the National Assembly. Bravo, Kocho! Well, to tell you the truth, I was moved to tears of joy. I almost came up to you and kissed you in front of all the deputies. But they would start stomping their feet at me, objecting... Do you remember which speech? How could you not? The whole world is talking about it. But you are right, Kocho! For so many thousands of voters not to go and tear apart twenty gendarmes and a drunken gang of fifty. Big deal! The gendarmes would have shot a hundred voters at most! Well, is that such a big deal? All in all, about two hundred houses would have gone into mourning. Let’s say, next Sunday the army comes and they shoot, they kill at most, at most three hundred people. How many houses of orphans—five hundred houses! Quite a business!...

Well, those rascals, they started taming the crowd, making sure not a hair falls! How can you not be outraged?... Thanks to such soft-hearted rascals, you waited a full eight years in Halki... To write them so many poems about stars and sighs, and for them to make you wait eight years. Eight years! A shame for the Bulgarian people. If at least a hundred thousand voters from all over Bulgaria had gone under the bullets, you could have taken your current cozy spot much earlier. But what a worthless people! Cowards! What the hell is this legality and freedom for, if at least a thousand voters aren't exterminated?... Hold on, dear Kocho, I like you this way. Give such speeches more often, to inspire greater trust in the big shots... and then look after your own pleasure! That the young generation would be indignant, that the people would be agitated — don't you even blink! The people! The people are a herd, once you swing the stick at them... And finally, am I the one to teach you these things!...

I am most glad that it was you who rushed to give this speech; no one could beat you to it. Truly, if you haven't inspired confidence in them by now, when will you ever!... All the notables are praising you! "Bravo," they say, "Kocho has become one of us; he’s finally come to his senses." Keep your wits about you now, stay on this path, and have no fear!... But always see to it, Kocho, put some money aside, for one never knows—the world is as fleeting as a blossom!

Kocho, when you read this letter - tear it up, so it doesn't fall into the hands of that fellow who described me traveling through Europe, lest he splash me across the pages somewhere again. I heard him the other day, talking to someone: “Well, what a shame, I didn't expect those words at all from our Velichkov”... - and I listen to him and wonder at his mind. He’s a scatterbrain... Kocho, man, why are you still publishing that wretched “Progress”? Drop it! Truth be told, even its name is so childish, it no longer suits a solid man like you. And if you're so itching to write - go ahead and write, but it would be most fitting to call the newspaper “It is not the time” and then our partisans would be called not-the-time-ists.
I brought a few vials in my saddlebags. Can’t you cook up some little law to have public buildings sprinkled with rose oil?
